items.title: [None][feat] Add lightweight per-pool KV cache utilization logging
items.body:
## Description

The aggregate `kv_cache_util` iteration log can hide a nearly full KV pool. Add `TLLM_KV_POOL_LOG_INTERVAL=N` to inspect GPU and host pools without enabling iteration performance statistics.

With `print_iter_log: true`, V2 uses a lightweight CPU-side GPU capacity snapshot on every logged iteration, including when the interval is disabled. Sampled iterations reuse that snapshot for GPU pool values and read host counters once. The interval defaults to `0` (disabled); use `50` for periodic samples or `1` for every iteration. Existing rank filtering applies. Warmup skips pool samples, repeated iteration numbers are sampled only once, and unsampled lines omit pool fields. Legacy managers retain their existing aggregate log.

The interval is validated at construction; empty means disabled. A warning explains when the setting cannot take effect. The cache manager logs the cold pool mapping at construction alongside the existing GPU mapping because GPU and host pool IDs are independent. Disk capacity is excluded; missing host tiers and zero-capacity pools report `N/A`.

- GPU utilization: `1 - (free + evictable) / total`, aggregated by slot count.
- Host occupancy: `1 - free / total`, including evictable cached pages.

```text
kv_cache_util = 0.600, kv_cache_gpu_pool_util = [0:0.900;1:0.500], kv_cache_host_pool_util = [0:0.750],
```

The diagnostic does not collect/reset iteration deltas or add CUDA synchronization or cross-rank communication. Sampling can miss transient peaks; formatting and log output still have a cost. No measured performance improvement is claimed.

## Test Coverage

- Added 23 CPU test cases covering GPU/host capacity semantics, independent groups, disk exclusion, missing/zero capacity, construction mapping, snapshot reuse, sampling deduplication, warmup, disabled/V1 behavior, interval validation, and log/rank filtering.
- All 23 passed in an isolated Python 3.12 harness on macOS with native/GPU imports stubbed. The harness loads the production profiling module and extracts the production KV methods; it validates Python control flow and counter reads, not native integration or the normal TensorRT-LLM pytest environment.
- Python compilation and `git diff --check` passed. The final documentation/comment correction preserves executable Python behavior; applicable pre-commit and DCO hooks passed.
- Pending: run `pytest tests/unittest/_torch/executor/test_kv_cache_utilization_log.py` in the TensorRT-LLM environment, a GPU inference smoke test, and an overhead A/B with identical workload/log/rank settings and interval `0` versus `50`.

## PR Checklist

- [x] Reviewed the applicable checklist: scoped change, documentation and regression coverage included, no new dependencies, no LLM argument/schema changes, and no ownership or architecture changes.

items.title: [None][feat] Support attention DP in KV cache connectors
items.body:
## Description

The generic KV connector previously assumed that every rank handled the same requests: rank 0 made scheduler decisions, and transfer completion waited for all workers. ADP owners can process different requests and issue different numbers of allocation callbacks, so those connector collectives cannot be used for ADP.

This change creates a connector scheduler adapter and worker on every ADP rank. Lookup, allocation feedback, transfer metadata and completion follow the local request owner. All adapters can connect to one shared logical storage pool and reuse compatible KV content produced by other owners. For example, an owner handling three requests can complete its transfers without requiring connector callbacks from an idle peer. The existing TP path retains rank-0 scheduling and completion across all attention shards.

### Changes

- Require both scheduler and worker classes to declare `supports_attention_dp = True`; instantiate adapters on every ADP rank. Existing third-party connectors remain gated until they implement this contract.
- Add `SchedulerOutput.attention_dp_rank` to identify the owner of local block IDs. Keep reusable content keys independent of the ADP rank.
- Remove cross-owner connector broadcasts and completion collectives under ADP. Request and transfer state remain local to each adapter.
- Exclude compute dummy requests from connector lookup, allocation feedback, metadata and request-finished callbacks. If asynchronous loading empties an owner's batch, attempt late dummy padding while preserving the real transfer plan.
- Defer cancellation of tracked asynchronous transfers until worker completion, and retire per-request connector metadata after the finish callback.
- Update the persistent-cache example to share a filesystem directory across owners, use stable SHA-256 keys over the complete prefix and cache salt, and atomically publish completed files.
- Add ownership, idle-owner, completion, cancellation and shared-pool regressions, plus a two-GPU serving regression covering balanced and unequal-length batches with overlap enabled and disabled.

### Scope

Initial support uses the V1 cache manager, one primary GPU pool, one attention worker per ADP owner, PP=1, CP=1, beam width 1 and guaranteed-no-evict scheduling. Existing exclusions for VSWA, internal host offload and Mamba/hybrid state remain. V2, heterogeneous attention shards and elastic peer-HBM allocation require separate integration.

items.title: [https://nvbugs/6732123][fix] Correct V2 KV cache quota estimation
items.body:
@coderabbitai summary

## Description

Fix three V2 KV cache sizing failures in one PR: PARD's separate draft pool can be too small to allocate or resume, GPT-OSS with finite window overrides can report hundreds of GiB of mandatory fixed cache, and layer-wise hybrid benchmarks can underallocate attention pages for their synthetic requests.

- Share context, generation-headroom, and SWA boundary-page accounting between static estimation and runtime quota conversion. Preserve the external drafter's fixed pool and page-rounded resume capacity. Estimate the standalone draft cost directly when splitting target/draft budgets.
- Keep the existing `CacheCost(slope, intercept)` model. Explicit native `full_attention` layers contribute to the slope even when a runtime window override bounds retention; native SWA and external draft pools retain fixed costs. Runtime windows are unchanged. No separate budget-estimation mode or `for_budget_split` parameter is needed. Configured target/draft quotas still sum to the input budget.
- Set `avg_seq_len=max_seq_len` in the layer-wise benchmark, where every dummy request actually has that length. Keep this workload correction in the benchmark rather than changing the hybrid pool solver.

PARD/DFlash allocation and resume regressions run in the GPU unit-test lane. The focused Nemotron/Qwen3-Next benchmark cases select V2 directly, without adding duplicate V1 CI cases. This PR incorporates the fixes from #18932 and #18954.

The native-full classification relies on explicit layer metadata; configs without it retain existing behavior. This is a static affine estimate, not an exact saturation curve for arbitrary all-SWA workloads.

The SWA context and boundary-page reservations also apply to ordinary target models with speculative decoding disabled. For a Gemma3-27B-shaped configuration (30 SWA layers at window 1024, 10 full-attention layers, 2048 bytes/token/layer, 64-token blocks, batch size 8, and `max_num_tokens=8192`), the fixed cost with scratch reuse disabled increases from 480 MiB (~0.47 GiB) to 990 MiB (~0.97 GiB): 480 MiB for context capacity and 30 MiB for retained boundary pages. Lower estimated token capacity under the same GPU memory budget is an expected consequence of correcting the earlier underestimation. Static estimation reads scratch reuse from `KvCacheConfig` and keeps it disabled for draft managers, matching runtime.

## Test Coverage

- Merged main at `e13e487195`; the related suite passed again on the merged revision: **142 passed**. Main removed the Llama-3.1-8B accuracy suite in #18809, including the old PARD overlap cases; this PR preserves that removal and retains the CUDA-backed PARD/DFlash quota regressions.
- CI lane correction: moved both CUDA-backed external-draft regressions out of the module-level `cpu_only` estimator file into `test_kv_cache_manager_v2.py`. Existing H100/B300/GB300 executor entries cover that file with `-m "not cpu_only"`; adding a GPU marker alone would not cancel an inherited CPU marker. Validated the CI marker expressions on B200: **40 passed, 54 deselected** with CUDA hidden and `-m cpu_only`; **54 passed, 3 deselected** with `-m "not cpu_only"`, including both PARD and DFlash regressions with no skips.
- Final combined budget split, cache estimation, V2 manager, and focused hybrid/MTP suite on B200: **142 passed**, including GPU allocation tests.
- All commit hooks passed, including modern and legacy Python lint/format checks.
- Regression tests use the estimated quota to allocate real PARD/DFlash context and generation caches, sweep unaligned page boundaries, then suspend and resume them. Replaying the pre-fix PARD estimator makes the same test fail at actual cache growth (`resize(1035, 1024)`); the current estimator passes.
- GPT-OSS budget coverage checks conservation and target/draft capacity bounds in three representative scenarios, without asserting exact affine coefficients or split ratios. Removed the Cartesian formula-comparison matrix and redundant internal page-count checks; test cleanup removes 146 net lines from the previous revision.
- B200 GPT-OSS 20B TP2 proxy: startup and two generation rounds passed with overlap both on and off. The proxy uses a compatible 120B Eagle3 draft checkpoint and disables CUDA graphs; it is a capacity check, not an accuracy evaluation. Full PARD accuracy and the original GPT-OSS 120B case have not been rerun for this combined revision.
- Focused V2 layer-wise benchmarks: Nemotron completed successfully. The combined run hit its 15-minute timeout while Qwen3-Next was still in first-time CUDA kernel compilation (`ptxas`); Qwen3-Next validation is incomplete, with no runtime quota result from this run.

- [x] Changes follow the coding guidelines and include regression coverage.

items.title: [None][fix] Size the FlashInfer page-index buffer for VSWA on V1 KV cache
items.body:
## Description

`FlashInferAttentionMetadata._post_init_with_buffers` read
`kv_cache_manager.blocks_in_primary_pool` directly to seed `max_num_blocks`,
which sizes the flat `_paged_kv_indices` buffer and the per-pool VSWA buffers.
That scalar is not part of the KV cache manager interface:

* `KVCacheManagerV2` always exposes it as a property.
* The V1 `KVCacheManager` only assigns it when it ends up with a single pool.
  The VSWA sizing path (`calculate_max_num_blocks_for_vswa()`) fills the
  `blocks_per_window` dict instead and leaves the scalar unset, as the standing
  `FIXME` next to it in `pyexecutor/resource_manager.py` already notes ("only
  covers the single window case and not VSWA scheme").

Any VSWA model routed to a V1 manager therefore dies in metadata construction
with:

```
AttributeError: 'KVCacheManager' object has no attribute 'blocks_in_primary_pool'
```

Disaggregated serving is one such route: `llm_utils.py` keeps a model's V2
preference only for the NIXL + Python-transceiver combination and otherwise
falls back to V1, so a VSWA model that runs fine aggregated crashes as soon as a
cache transceiver is configured.

The fix routes the read through a small `_get_blocks_in_primary_pool()` helper:

* use `blocks_in_primary_pool` when the manager exposes it (V2, single-pool V1);
* otherwise take the largest primary count from `blocks_per_window`. That is an
  upper bound across the pools, so the buffer stays large enough for every
  pool, and it feeds the same `max_num_blocks` seed that the per-layer buffer
  sizes are folded into;
* raise a named `AttributeError` describing both missing attributes when
  neither is available, instead of an anonymous attribute read.

This matches the `getattr`-guarded V2-only lookups a few lines further down in
the same function ("V1 managers lack the per-pool infrastructure"). The
`FIXME` in `resource_manager.py` is left in place; its other point
(single-window-only semantics of the scalar) still stands.

## Test Coverage

Unit test (CPU-only, stub managers):

`tests/unittest/_torch/attention/test_flashinfer_attention.py::TestFlashInferAttention::test_blocks_in_primary_pool_falls_back_to_blocks_per_window`

* a V2-shaped manager returns the scalar even when a `blocks_per_window` table
  is also present;
* a V1 VSWA-shaped manager (no scalar, three windows) returns the largest
  per-window primary count;
* a manager with neither attribute, or an empty `blocks_per_window`, raises an
  `AttributeError` that names the manager type and the missing attributes.

The failure this fixes was first hit in disaggregated serving of a VSWA model
whose class prefers the V2 KV cache manager but was demoted to V1: engine setup
aborted during metadata construction with the `AttributeError` above. This
change removes that crash by sizing the buffer from the per-window table when
the scalar is absent; the guard itself is covered by the unit test above.

## PR Checklist

- PR description clearly explains what and why. If using CodeRabbit's summary, please make sure it makes sense.
- PR Follows [TRT-LLM CODING GUIDELINES](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/CODING_GUIDELINES.md) to the best of your knowledge.
- Test cases are provided for new code paths (see [test instructions](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/tree/main/tests#1-how-does-the-ci-work))
- If PR introduces API changes, an appropriate PR label is added - either `api-compatible` or `api-breaking`. For `api-breaking`, include `BREAKING` in the PR title.
- Any new dependencies have been scanned for license and vulnerabilities
- [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) updated if ownership changes
- Documentation updated as needed
- Update [tava architecture diagram](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/.github/tava_architecture_diagram.md) if there is a significant design change in PR.
- The reviewers assigned automatically/manually are appropriate for the PR.

items.title: [#18849][fix] Pass vocab_size to hybrid-Mamba KV cache managers
items.body:
## Description

Fixes https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/issues/18849.

`_create_kv_cache_manager` passed `vocab_size=config.vocab_size` on the MLA branch and the plain-attention branch only. The three hybrid-Mamba branches (Kimi K3 / KDA, `nemotron_hybrid`, and `qwen3_next` / Qwen3.5 / Qwen4-Exp) constructed the manager without it, and `MambaHybridCacheManagerV2` absorbs unknown keywords through `**kwargs`, so `KVCacheManagerV2.vocab_size` silently stayed `None`.

That field is read only when building multimodal block-reuse cache keys (`_augment_tokens_with_mm_run_metadata` / `_augment_tokens_with_contiguous_mm_metadata`), which is why a hybrid deployment serves text-only traffic indefinitely and then dies on its first `image_url` request: `gen_multimodal_cache_key_tokens()` receives `None` as `id_offset`, the resulting `TypeError` escapes into the PyExecutor event loop, and every rank is hard-killed.

Two changes:

1. `vocab_size` moves into `manager_extra_kwargs`, which is already gated on `issubclass(kv_cache_manager_cls, KVCacheManagerV2)`, and the two per-branch `vocab_size=config.vocab_size` arguments are removed. Every V2 branch now gets the value from one place, so a branch added later cannot omit it — the same reasoning `_mamba_conv_layout_kwargs` already applies to `conv_state_layout`. The V1 managers are unaffected: `KVCacheManager` swallowed the argument into `**kwargs` without reading it, and `MixedMambaHybridCacheManager` (which has no `**kwargs`) must not receive it.
2. The new `_resolve_vocab_size` helper falls back to `text_config.vocab_size`, because composite VLM configs keep the field on the nested text config.

Additionally, `KVCacheManagerV2._augment_tokens_for_block_reuse` now raises a `RuntimeError` naming the missing construction argument when it is asked to build multimodal cache keys without a `vocab_size`, rather than letting `None` reach the binding. Text-only requests return before that check, so they are unaffected.

Not addressed here, to keep this PR to one concern: suggestion 3 in the issue — failing the individual request with a 4xx instead of terminating the executor when multimodal metadata cannot be built (which also covers the `disable_mm_encoder: true` case). That is executor-level error classification and is worth its own PR, so it is now tracked separately in #18971.

I do not have Hopper hardware, so the end-to-end reproduction from the issue was not re-run; the reporter's verified workaround fills in the same value this change now passes.

## Test Coverage

`tests/unittest/_torch/executor/kv_cache/test_mamba_cache_manager.py`
- `test_hybrid_v2_manager_receives_vocab_size` — routes a Qwen3 hybrid config through `_create_kv_cache_manager` and asserts the V2 manager is constructed with `vocab_size`. Fails on `main`.
- `test_hybrid_v2_manager_reads_vocab_size_from_text_config` — same, with `vocab_size` only on the nested `text_config`.
- `test_hybrid_v1_manager_does_not_receive_vocab_size` — guards the V1 `MixedMambaHybridCacheManager`, whose signature has no `**kwargs`.

`tests/unittest/_torch/executor/kv_cache/test_kv_cache_v2_multimodal_runs.py`
- `test_augment_tokens_for_block_reuse_reports_missing_vocab_size` — the guard names the missing argument.
- `test_augment_tokens_for_block_reuse_ignores_missing_vocab_size_for_text` — text-only requests still work without a `vocab_size`.

Both files are CPU-only. `pre-commit`'s formatters and linters (ruff 0.9.4 check/format on the Group A files, yapf 0.43.0 / isort 5.12.0 / `ruff-legacy` on `_util.py`, codespell) pass on the changed files. The test cases themselves have not been executed — TensorRT-LLM does not build on the macOS host I am working from — so please run the two files in CI.

## PR Checklist

Please review the following before submitting your PR:
- PR description clearly explains what and why. If using CodeRabbit's summary, please make sure it makes sense.

items.title: [None][feat] Add calibrated INT8 KV cache to PyTorch backend
items.body:
## Summary

Add calibrated INT8 KV-cache storage to the PyTorch TRTLLM attention backend for dense decoder-only models with FP16/BF16 projections. `KvCacheConfig(dtype="int8")` reaches checkpoint loading, fused-QKV scale parameters, attention, and both KV-cache managers. This addresses the INT8 KV-cache item in #3701.

The unquantized fused-QKV weight path now has one cache-scale loading hook for INT8 and FP4. INT8 requires paired positive finite scalar `k_scale`/`v_scale` tensors, uses their maximum for the existing native shared K/V scale, and preserves scale pointers on reload. FP4 retains its optional per-K/V scale loading and environment opt-out; INT8 rejects `TRTLLM_LOAD_KV_SCALES=0` to prevent uncalibrated unity scales. Cache accounting, including V2 static fraction-based capacity estimation, uses one byte per INT8 element; allocator granularity still applies.

## Supported scope

Full prefill followed by single-token decode, paged cache storage, unquantized FP16/BF16 dense decoder projections, TRTLLM attention backend. Disable chunked prefill and prefix block reuse. Reject unsupported cached prefill, speculative decoding, MLA, sparse/cross attention, context parallelism, hybrid models, quantized projections, disaggregated serving, and KV connectors.

Decode-only calls skip the cached-context list scan. Tensor and cache-metadata guards remain per-call because a backend caller can replace its inputs after warmup; tests cover those replacements rather than caching the first validation result indefinitely.

## Shared FMHA prerequisite

Full prefill exposed a missing `cu_kv_seqlens` pointer in packed-QKV FMHA, also reproducible with FP16 cache. The pointer initialization remains a prerequisite in this PR. The new independent `test_packed_qkv_fmha.py` verifies FP16/BF16, MHA/GQA, and unequal context lengths against the Vanilla backend, and asserts the fallback packed-QKV path is actually selected without KV quantization.

These eight regression cases are registered explicitly for A10 and B200; H100 collects them through its existing `unittest/_torch/attention` directory entry. Stage mapping was checked. Only SM89 was executed on the remote RTX 4090; Hopper/Blackwell CI results are still required before merge. The native fix has not been split into another PR.

## Validation

On remote RTX 4090, PyTorch 2.12.0+cu130 and CUDA 13.0, at `e2a0a813cf53cbd7df8f83cb0754fd56d542df93`:

- 96 tests passed: 20 config/accounting, 20 scale-loading/compatibility, 46 INT8 attention, two full checkpoint/LLM tests, and eight independent full-precision FMHA cases.
- 81 existing cache estimation/budget regression tests passed.
- All 54 attention tests passed Compute Sanitizer with zero memory errors (`--report-api-errors no` suppresses import-time CUDA API probes).
- With CUDA devices hidden: 20 CPU tests passed, 76 CUDA-dependent tests skipped.
- New sizing/transfer-guard tests reproduced four failures on the previous implementation before the fixes.
- Full checkpoint tests use explicitly resolved INT8 with V1 and V2, exercise fraction-based capacity estimation, and compare eager versus CUDA Graph generation using the same cache dtype. They no longer require token equality between FP16 and INT8 caches.
- Full pre-commit and DCO commit hooks passed. Test-list AST validation and A10/H100/B200 stage mapping were checked.

Python changes use the previously rebuilt native libraries from this PR. That build compiled 101 affected objects, updated three static archives, and relinked the core library, Torch library and bindings. Unchanged objects/dependencies were reused from an existing rc26 build; it was not a clean full build. This update does not change native code. Multi-GPU and other GPU architectures have not been exercised by this validation.

## Quantization quality limitation

The native path uses a single shared scalar for K and V. The earlier Qwen2.5-0.5B calibration experiment exposed a roughly 603x K/V range mismatch in the first layer and degraded generated text with the shared scale. Additional checkpoint balancing was diagnostic only and is not shipped in this change. This review update does not establish model-quality acceptance or serving speedup. Checkpoint scales must be calibrated for INT8, including rotary K ranges, and model quality requires representative evaluation.

## Dev Engineer Review

Cache Manager V2 now accounts for standalone draft managers and PARD runtime headroom. Budget splitting preserves separate target and draft affine costs, including SWA, retained pages, rounding, and resume costs. Shared headroom logic applies to estimation, quota conversion, allocation growth, and `max_blocks_per_seq`. The generic `CacheCost` model remains unchanged. Main regression risk is inconsistency between static sizing and runtime allocation for uncommon speculative-decoding configurations.

Four KV-cache unit-test files and one integration test file changed. Coverage includes PARD headroom, affine budget splitting, SWA and rounding costs, draft-cache reuse, resume behavior, quota expectations, and maximum block capacity. The reported 329 KV-cache V2 tests pass. `test_pard` is listed in both the QA list and the `l0_h100` CI list. Coverage verdict: **sufficient**.

### Per-File QA Perspective

- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/pyexecutor/_util.py`: Verify target and draft cost estimation with standalone and one-model draft layouts, configured token limits, SWA fixed costs, and GPU-budget error reporting.
- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/pyexecutor/kv_cache/kv_cache_manager_v2.py`: Verify consistent speculative headroom across static estimation, runtime growth, draft reservations, block limits, SWA, rounding, and resume behavior.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/executor/kv_cache/test_kv_cache_budget_split.py`: Covers explicit draft intercepts, slot inflation, boundary/context blocks, and fixed-cost allocation. This unit test is not an integration test-list entry.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/executor/kv_cache/test_kv_cache_estimation.py`: Covers sliding-window allocation, speculative decoding, draft reuse, PARD/DFLASH cost derivation, resume utilization, and generation headroom. This unit test is not an integration test-list entry.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/executor/kv_cache/test_kv_cache_manager_v2.py`: Covers PARD manager capacity, generation headroom, and ledger-block rounding across cache tiers. This unit test is not an integration test-list entry.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

Cache manager V2 could under-size the standalone draft KV pool used by one-engine external drafters such as PARD. A logical PARD draft length of K consumes 2K runtime tokens per generation step; for K=4, the maximum KV capacity lead is `(K - 1) + 2K = 11` tokens.

This change keeps KV cost accounting purely affine (`slope * tokens + intercept`) while making the estimator match runtime allocation geometry:

- estimate the standalone draft manager directly and preserve its independent slope/intercept when splitting target and draft budgets;
- use the same speculative-generation headroom for estimation, quota conversion, allocation growth, and `max_blocks_per_seq`;
- include fixed SWA context/generation capacity, retained boundary pages, page-granularity rounding, and the resume watermark in the manager-owned intercept.

The generic `CacheCost` model is unchanged; manager-specific pool geometry remains encapsulated in the V2 estimator.

The one-model target/draft joint-reuse fix now present on `main` is also required for correct PARD block-reuse behavior and acceptance length. The PARD integration results below validate the combined behavior after rebasing onto that fix; they do not attribute the acceptance-length improvement to this accounting change alone.

- Relevant KV cache V2 unit suites: `329 passed`
- Llama 3.1 8B PARD integration test, forced cache manager V2 with block reuse enabled:
  - overlap enabled: accuracy `73.92`, average accepted length `3.357`

- Added focused coverage for:
  - PARD K=4's 11-token generation headroom;

  - `max_blocks_per_seq` covering PARD generation capacity.

## Description

This is non-functional change. Only adding assertion for code completeness.

V2's disaggregated KV transfer builds peer pointers as `base + stride * slot_id` from

items.title: [None][feat] Merge back locality domain support for KV cache and two-stream attention
items.body:
> Merge-back from the internal Rubin feature branch, sliced by path. This slice is the
> KV cache runtime layer plus the locality-domain two-stream attention path.

## Description

A locality domain splits a GPU into halves with their own memory. This adds:

- **KV cache runtime** — slot allocation, free-slot preparation, page indexing
  and eviction take a `locality_domain_id`; GPU storage backs each domain with its own
  physical memory. Existing callers move to keyword arguments so the new parameter
  cannot bind positionally.
- **Two-stream attention** (`attention/backends/trtllm.py`) — each domain runs on its
  own stream; per-domain metadata,
  workspaces, block offsets and KV lengths; the batch is sorted by domain so each
  domain's slice is contiguous.
- **Model engine / py_executor** — requests are assigned a domain and reordered by it;
  `attn_metadata` carries the per-domain request/token split points; CUDA graph warmup
  gives each active domain one max-length dummy request.
- **`thop/cublasScaledMM.cpp`** — the cuBLAS wrapper is keyed by `CUcontext`, since each
  domain runs under its own green context.

Locality domains are Python-backend only. On the C++ backend
`enable_locality_domains=True` raises `NotImplementedError` rather than silently
returning a non-localized cache.

Also fixes `pool_group_descs`, which called `num_slots()` without a domain id and made
locality-domain startup fail outright. `base_address` is slot 0's address, which lives
in domain 0, so the slot count now describes the same domain.

**Not included:** `modules/linear.py` and `models/modeling_deepseekv3.py` (MLA). Those
are a separate internal MR, so locality domains are not exercisable on MLA models yet.

## Test Coverage

`tests/unittest/kv_cache_manager_v2_tests/` — allocation, resize, suspend/resume,
eviction filtering, salted reuse, page indexing, non-localized backward compatibility.
`tests/integration/defs/kv_cache/test_stream_localization_e2e.py` — localized vs
baseline output equivalence.
`tests/unittest/_torch/executor/test_pytorch_model_engine.py` — CUDA graph warmup
request split.

Verified on GB200 with mock localization (`num_domains=2`, `fork_join=True`): greedy
output byte-identical to the non-localized baseline. Green contexts and real VMM
behaviour need Rubin and are not covered here.

## PR Checklist

- [x] PR title follows the format
- [x] Tests added/updated
- [x] Documentation not required

items.title: [None][perf] reuse emptied host KV cache slots before eviction
items.body:
## Problem this solves

When a KV-cache block is onboarded from secondary storage, `WindowBlockManager::onboardBlock` copies its content into a fresh primary block and swaps the two blocks' memory-pool offsets. The original secondary slot is therefore left empty.

Today that empty slot is returned at the default retention priority and appended to the back of the secondary LRU queue. `LRUEvictionPolicy::getFreeBlock(kSecondaryLevel)` selects the front of the lowest non-empty priority queue, so the allocator can evict every reusable host block ahead of the empty slot before it reaches the slot that contains no data at all. Each onboard can effectively remove one host slot from useful capacity for an entire LRU rotation.

This shows up in long-context, multi-turn agent workloads that repeatedly onboard old prefixes while concurrently offloading newer prefixes. Despite having empty secondary slots, the cache can evict live host content and later recompute those long-gap prefixes.

## What changes

After the onboard swap, this PR returns the emptied secondary slot at minimum retention priority and at the front of its free queue:

```cpp
block->setPriority(executor::KvCacheRetentionConfig::kMinRetentionPriority);
mEvictionPolicy->releaseBlock(block, /*toFront=*/true);
```

The next offload therefore fills the empty slot before evicting host content that is still eligible for reuse. This is the same reclaim-first principle already used when detached blocks are returned to the eviction policy.

The production behavior is two statements. The surrounding comment documents why both the priority and queue position matter.

This change is deliberately isolated to the empty-slot lifecycle. It does not include prefix-walk, scheduler, quantization, kernel, or configuration changes.

## Why this is safe

At this point in `onboardBlock`, `block` is the fresh primary block returned by `getFreeBlock`, after its memory-pool offset has been swapped with the onboarded block:

- it contains no reusable KV-cache content;
- it has no references;
- it is detached from the reuse lookup tree;
- `getFreeBlock` has already cleared any duration associated with its prior use.

Minimum retention priority correctly describes an empty slot: there is no content to retain. When the slot is selected for a later offload, `claimBlock` resets its retention metadata before new content is installed. Consequently, the slot does not acquire stale expiration behavior.

The transfer and synchronization sequence is unchanged. The copy completes through the existing transfer manager, offsets are swapped at the same point, and the slot is released only afterward. `WindowBlockManager::offloadBlock` continues to return the emptied primary slot through its existing path.

KV-cache events also become more accurate: the onboard and subsequent offload still emit their cache-level update events, but there is no removal event for a reusable host block because no reusable host block was evicted.

## Tests

The new regression test constructs four primary and four secondary blocks, then:

1. allocates a three-block sequence;
2. offloads its first block and records the secondary memory-pool slot;
3. onboards that block, leaving the recorded secondary slot empty;
4. offloads a second live block;
5. verifies that the second block lands in the recorded empty slot;
6. verifies queue integrity and that the offloaded block retains its own normal priority.

Without this fix, step 5 fails because the allocator selects an unused slot farther back in the default-priority queue. With the fix, it selects the just-emptied minimum-priority slot first.

The existing KV-cache event-stream test is also updated to expect one onboard and one offload event with no removal event for this sequence.

Validation performed:

- `BlockManagerOnboardReleasesEmptiedHostSlotFirst` passed on a CUDA-enabled build of the same change.
- Filtered `kvCacheManagerTest` suite: 189/189 passed on that CUDA-enabled build.
- `pre-commit run clang-format --files cpp/tensorrt_llm/batch_manager/kvCacheManager.cpp cpp/tests/unit_tests/batch_manager/kvCacheManagerTest.cpp` passed on this `main` port.
- `git diff --check` passed.

The CUDA suite has not been rerun locally on this exact `main` commit because the development host used for the port has no NVIDIA GPU. CI should rerun the C++ unit suite against current `main`.

## Cache-retention and performance evidence

The issue was found with DRAM KV offload under a long-context, multi-turn agent trace whose returning prompts frequently reuse hundreds of thousands of tokens. Runtime/replay analysis showed that approximately 45-51% of secondary slots could be empty on average while long-idle continuations still lost reusable host prefixes. That combination is inconsistent with a capacity-only explanation and matches the queue-rotation mechanism above.

In an isolated same-node A/B at fixed offered work, changing only the empty-slot reclaim behavior produced:

| Metric | Existing behavior | Reclaim empty slot first | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Long-gap achieved/offered prefix reuse | 97.58% | 99.93% | +2.35 percentage points |
| Effective input throughput per GPU | baseline | 1.0093x baseline | +0.93% |
| Short-gap prefix reuse | unchanged | unchanged | no regression |

The throughput cell was client-paced and already close to its maximum attainable reuse, so the direct throughput delta is intentionally reported as a bounded result, not a universal expectation. The larger practical benefit is avoiding a cache/TTFT cliff as each prefill worker carries more concurrent long-context sessions: reclaiming empty slots preserves useful host residency and lets the configured host tier behave closer to its nominal capacity.

Profiling found no material change in GPU kernel families, as expected for an eviction-order fix. The improvement appeared in the host resource-preparation path: previously exposed onboard/admission work was substantially reduced after long-gap prefix retention recovered.


### Replay and full-workload context

A block-level retention replay driven by the measured request reuse-distance distribution and host-pool geometry reproduced the stock long-gap loss. With reclaim-first ordering, it projected long-gap achieved/offered prefix reuse of **97.9% at 6 prefill workers** and **94.9% at 5 prefill workers**. This is mechanism and capacity-pressure evidence, not a standalone throughput benchmark.

The host-slot-only A/B above deliberately measures this PR in isolation. Two additional full, concurrency-227 GLM-5.2 AgentX measurements tested whether the corrected host path survived sustained load. They held scheduler configuration and topology fixed while moving from the configuration-only executable to an executable containing both this change and the linear prefix-reuse walk from [#17848](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/17848):

| Disaggregated topology | TPS/GPU, before | TPS/GPU, combined code | Change | Total backend TPS | p90 TPS/user | TTFT p90 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 6P + 1D, decode EP8 | 33,668.13 | 36,717.90 | **+9.06%** | 1,077,380 to 1,174,973 | 84.995 to 84.747 | not isolated |
| 5P + 1D, decode EP8 | 35,237.05 | 41,522.73 | **+17.84%** | 986,637 to 1,162,636 | 80.923 to 85.286 | 12.34 s to 3.30 s |

These full-load deltas are **combined-stack evidence**, not standalone attribution to this PR: they include #17848 and interaction between faster admission, retained host capacity, and load per prefill worker. A smaller proxy isolated #17848 at +3.54% on top of the same scheduler setting, but that number must not simply be subtracted from the table because the two fixes interact. The defensible isolated attribution for this PR remains the host-slot-only result above: +2.35 percentage points of long-gap reuse and +0.93% effective input TPS/GPU in the already client-paced cell.

Matched Nsight profiles support the host-side mechanism. No material GPU kernel-family change appeared. Instead, exposed `prepare_resources` time fell from **4.9 ms to 0.2 ms**, while `_prepare_inputs` p90 fell from approximately **81-170 ms to 26-37 ms** across the observed windows as repeated host onboarding/admission stalls disappeared.

## Relationship to existing eviction work and duplicate audit

This change extends the reclaim-first rule already merged in [#11685](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/11685). That PR sends detached blocks released at request completion to the front of the free queue. It does not cover `onboardBlock`: after the memory-pool offset swap, this path directly calls `releaseBlock(block)` without the detached-block ordering used by `releaseBlocks`. The empty secondary slot can therefore remain behind live reusable host blocks despite #11685.

Current `main` at `ba32790910d126c72ad426e1ddc88c15974adf01` still contains that default-priority, back-of-queue release. Commit history and blame show no later change to this onboard lifecycle.

All ten other open PRs that touch `kvCacheManager.cpp` or its header were also inspected for an equivalent fix. None changes this host-tier release behavior. The closest overlap is [#16252](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/16252), which gives newly introduced disk-tier empty slots minimum priority, but its existing host-tier `onboardBlock` branch still uses the unchanged `releaseBlock(block)` call. Other open work touching onboarding, transfer preparation, radix-tree eviction, or cache events likewise leaves this lifecycle gap open.

## Functional and performance impact

- **Correctness:** no KV contents, offsets, copy ordering, or reference ownership changes.
- **Eviction policy:** only empty secondary slots are moved ahead of retained secondary content.
- **Events:** a later offload no longer reports removal of live host content when an empty slot is available.
- **Performance:** neutral when the secondary tier is unused or has no reuse pressure; positive when onboard/offload churn would otherwise strand empty slots behind retained blocks.
- **Memory:** no allocation-size or capacity change.

## Diff size

Against current `main`:

| Scope | Insertions | Deletions |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Production | 11 | 2 |
| Tests | 85 | 5 |
| Total | 96 | 7 |

Only two production statements change behavior; the remaining production additions explain the queue and retention rules.

## Limitations

- The measured A/B used DRAM secondary storage. The lifecycle correction is common to other local secondary transfer modes, but they were not separately benchmarked.
- The gain depends on workload reuse distance and host-tier pressure. Workloads without onboarding or with a cold/unused host tier should not be expected to improve.
- This PR does not alter host-cache sizing or admission policy; it makes existing secondary capacity reusable in the correct order.

items.title: [None][fix] Emit multimodal keys in KV cache v2 events

labels.name: api-compatible
labels.description: Accepted LLM API contract change that is backwards-compatible

items.body:
## Description

KV cache manager v2 stored events currently omit multimodal keys. Generate `mm_keys` directly from the actual cached block's native digest and continuation tokens in both the C++ and Python event managers. Each key contains the item digest and item-local start offset, including items spanning blocks and runs separated by text.

Radix blocks retain the latest prefix digest when MM event decoding is enabled, so event generation reads the direct parent's context without walking the ancestor chain. The immutable digest remains valid across detach/reattach and does not retain ancestor blocks or pages. Complete MM keys belong to the event payload. Forward the vocabulary offset through ordinary and hybrid V2 manager construction.

V2 emits the item digest as a hexadecimal string. Optional UUIDs continue to participate in upstream item hashing with the content; V1 still exposes an original UUID when supplied. Token encoding and block hashing are unchanged. The block context adds a shared-pointer field even when events are disabled; digest-context maintenance is enabled only when needed for events.

items.title: [None][feat] Add DeepSeek-V4 support to NVFP4 cold-page KV Cache Compression
items.body:
## Summary

This PR extends NVFP4 cold-page KV cache compression to the cache layout used by DeepSeek-V4 sparse Attention.

DeepSeek-V4 does not store one conventional K/V tensor per Attention layer. It maintains several cache components with different formats and purposes. This change compresses only the ordinary ratio-4 compressed sparse-attention (CSA) latent that benefits from NVFP4, while preserving the remaining components in their existing representation.

The active GPU cache and the DeepSeek-V4 Attention path are unchanged. NVFP4 conversion occurs only when KVCM V2 moves a Page from the GPU hot tier to the Host or Disk cold tier; onboarding restores the original BF16 or FP8 runtime layout before the Page is published back to the model.

## DeepSeek-V4 cache structure and compression policy

| Cache component | TensorRT-LLM role | Runtime format | Cold-page format |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SWA history | `deepseek_v4_swa` | BF16 / per-tensor FP8 | Lossless |
| Ratio-4 CSA NoPE | `deepseek_v4_compress[0:448]` | BF16 / per-tensor FP8 | NVFP4 |
| Ratio-4 CSA RoPE | `deepseek_v4_compress[448:512]` | BF16 / per-tensor FP8 | Lossless |
| CSA Indexer-K | `deepseek_v4_indexer_compress` | Blockwise FP8 / MXFP4 | Lossless |
| Ratio-128 HCA | `deepseek_v4_compress` | BF16 / per-tensor FP8 | Lossless |
| Compressor state | `deepseek_v4_*compressor_{kv,score}` | FP32 | Lossless |

Weight precision is independent of this policy. The table describes runtime cache storage, not model weights.

The special `fp8_ds_mla` footer-scale hot layout is not interpreted as an ordinary 512-element FP8 row. This PR rejects that layout during codec construction instead of risking silent corruption. The supported DeepSeek-V4 source layouts are ordinary BF16 and per-tensor FP8 cache rows.

## Cold-page layout

For a provider-owned DeepSeek-V4 lifecycle, the codec produces one fixed-size, 16-byte-aligned opaque cold Page. Conceptually, its sections are:

```text
one KVCM lifecycle Page
+--------------------------+
| CSA NoPE E2M1 values     |  448 values per CSA row, two values per byte
+--------------------------+
| CSA block-16 E4M3 scales |  one scale for every 16 NoPE values
+--------------------------+
| CSA RoPE suffix          |  original 64 values per row, copied losslessly
+--------------------------+
| CSA Indexer-K            |  original packed bytes and scales
+--------------------------+
| colocated HCA data       |  original bytes when HCA shares the lifecycle
+--------------------------+
| 16-byte alignment        |
+--------------------------+
```

For the production ratio-4 geometry with a 128-token KVCM Page, one CSA Page contains 32 compressed entries. The transformed NoPE section occupies 7,168 bytes of E2M1 data plus 896 bytes of block scales. The RoPE suffix remains in the source runtime type, and Indexer-K remains in its original packed format.

Independent KVCM lifecycles are not merged. “One cold-page layout” means one opaque cold blob for each Page of one KVCM lifecycle. SWA and transient compressor lifecycles continue through KVCM's default lossless codec. When ratio-4 CSA and ratio-128 HCA persistent layers share a lifecycle, the provider owns that complete lifecycle, compresses only CSA NoPE, and copies HCA losslessly.

## Implementation

- Recognize the public DeepSeek-V4 KVCM buffer roles and map each synthetic CSA lifecycle back to its model layer.
- Extend the existing metadata-driven NVFP4 kernel path to support a quantized prefix in a strided row: `head_dim = 448`, `row_stride = 512`.
- Fuse CSA NoPE quantization with GPU-to-Host transfer and fuse Host-to-GPU transfer with dequantization, using the existing Page-batched launcher.
- Copy the RoPE suffix and all other buffers owned by the same lifecycle losslessly within the same launch and cold Page.
- Reuse the model layer's optional ModelOpt K global scale. Use identity scaling when compatible metadata is absent or for an independent draft cache.
- Keep partial-Page handling unchanged: the codec transforms the complete physical Page, while KVCM remains responsible for the logical valid-token count.
- Fail closed for unknown or mixed DeepSeek-V4 roles, invalid geometry, incomplete scale metadata, and the unsupported `fp8_ds_mla` footer-scale layout.

This change does not modify DeepSeek-V4 Attention, model forward, active KV quantization, KVCM allocation or migration policy, the public cold-page codec ABI, or runtime storage ownership.

## Validation

- [x] 53 SM100 native CUDA layout and numerical tests, including BF16 and FP8 strided-prefix round trips, byte-exact suffix and side-buffer preservation, partial Pages, guard canaries, and batches larger than 256 Pages.
- [x] 48 focused Python tests for DeepSeek-V4 role discovery, ratio-4 CSA and ratio-128 HCA lifecycle ownership, exact offsets and cold-page sizes, per-model-layer K scales, lossless fallback, and fail-closed layouts.
- [x] Real KVCM V2 Host-migration tests for both BF16 and ordinary FP8 hot cache layouts, exercising `prefill -> suspend -> encode -> Host -> decode -> resume` with balanced, nonzero encode/decode Page counts.
- [x] Exact source, wheel, installed package, and native-library identity checks for the tested SM100 build.

## Limitation

This PR only targets DeepSeek V4 on Blackwell series (e.g. B200, GB300). Hopper chips are out of scope and not supported.

## Dev Engineer Review

- Commits only the stable generation prefix after sampling state and speculative KV relocation.

  - Added coverage for `include_finished_requests=True`.
  - Added coverage that skipping the target KV cache manager still updates draft and compression managers.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/executor/test_kv_cache_manager_v2.py`

No modified test functions were reported as covered in `tests/integration/test_lists/`. The changes provide focused unit coverage for commit boundaries, speculative relocation, token slicing, resource-manager behavior, and the TriAttention guard.

Verdict: sufficient.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

KVCacheManagerV2 stopped committing after prefill, so generation KV produced by decode was not retained in the reusable block index. For a multi-turn disaggregated request, the decode worker could reuse the original prompt but had to receive the previous turn's output KV again.

This change keeps `ALL_REUSABLE` V2 caches open after prefill and commits only the stable generation prefix after sampling state is applied and before response handling can remove the request. The newest sampled token is excluded because its KV is not materialized until the next forward pass. Accepted speculative KV relocation and history resize complete before commit. Generation commit remains disabled for draft caches and compression that manages physical history, preserving prompt-only reuse for TriAttention. Token collection uses a zero-copy view and materializes only the newly committed slice, avoiding an O(sequence length) Python-list conversion on every decode step.

The generic resource-manager update skips only the target V2 KV manager to avoid updating it twice while preserving draft KV and KV compression manager updates. This change does not modify the transfer-side prefix trimming algorithm or any public API.

items.title: [https://nvbugs/6701493][fix] Latch warmup peak before KV cache size estimation resets it
items.body:
## Summary
- **Root cause**: `KvCacheCreator.estimate_max_kv_cache_size()` calls `torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()` before its profiling pass, discarding the high-water mark left by warmup (torch.compile specialization, autotuning, CUDA-graph capture, pool pre-population) that already ran in `PyExecutor.__init__`. It then sizes the KV pool against only the text-only profiling dummy's peak, which is smaller than warmup's, so the pool absorbs memory that warmup will need again when it is replayed against the final cache. On Gemma3-27B-FP8 at the default `free_gpu_memory_fraction=0.9` this handed out 42.38 GiB and left ~7.2 GiB of torch headroom — too little for MMLU's 128-row × 262144-vocab fp32 logits, so the third eval OOMed.
- **Fix**: Capture `torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated()` into `warmup_peak_memory` immediately before the `empty_cache()` / `reset_peak_memory_stats()` pair, then take `max(post-profiling peak, warmup_peak_memory)` as `torch_peak_memory` when computing the available KV budget. This keeps the estimator honest about the true torch high-water mark instead of raising the model-side workaround (lowering `free_gpu_memory_fraction` / `max_batch_size` per test, as the passing bf16 sibling does), so every model benefits without per-test tuning; the CnnDailymail rouge1 check confirms the change is accuracy-neutral (28.756 vs 28.778 pre-fix baseline, threshold 25.910).
- **Original test**: `pytest tests/integration/defs/accuracy/test_llm_api_pytorch.py::TestGemma3_27BInstruct::test_fp8_prequantized -v`

items.title: [None][perf] Fuse MiniMax-M3 MSA per-layer KV-cache writes into one kernel
items.body: ## Description **Port of #16755 (merged on Minimax-m3 side branch for AgentX submission) to `main`. Same change, re-applied on top of main's MSA backend.** ### Where this PR targets at: MiniMax-M3 MSA per-layer KV-cache writes fusion (K, V, index-K): Take a sparse layer as example: 1. input RMSNorm 2. QKV proj  (+ index-Q/K proj for the indexer) 3. **►► WRITE: scatter new K, V, index-K into the paged caches   ◄◄ our fix** 4. indexer:  proxy-FMHA (reads index-K) → max-reduce → SelectBlocks (top-16 of 128-token blocks) 5. main sparse attention (reads K,V from selected blocks) → o_proj 6. post-attn RMSNorm 7. MoE FFN (router → top-4 experts + shared) + allreduce ### The problem Each MSA layer writes its new-token main K, main V, and (sparse layers) index-K. Writing of K, V and index-K takes four tiny kernels: division, remainder, index cast, index_put scatter. So that's 3*4=12 kernel launches per sparse layer. At 60 layers that is ~720 tiny kernels per decode step, all captured into decode CUDA graphs and re-executed on every step. It accumulates to large launch overhead. ### The fix This PR replaces them with **one Triton launch per layer** (~720 → 60) launches on the write path each iter). ### Measured impact (4x B300, InferenceMAX-style serving benchmark) `trtllm-serve` + `benchmark_serving`, NVFP4 + fp8 KV cache, MSA, decode CUDA graphs + overlap scheduler, no spec decode, random 8k/1k, identical seeded prompt sets, JIT/autotuner warmed. | metric | conc 64, TP4/EP4 | conc 32, TP2/EP1 | |---|---|---| | output throughput | 1,817.1 → 1,942.5 tok/s (**+6.9%**) | 1,082.1 → 1,171.7 tok/s (**+8.3%**) | | median TPOT (≈ decode iteration time) | 33.86 → 31.76 ms (**−2.1 ms**) | 28.39 → 26.20 ms (**−2.2 ms**) | | mean TTFT | 995 → 954 ms (−4.1%) | 715 → 690 ms (−3.5%) | ### Nsys trace for a layer (look at green parts) Before fix: 4 tiny kernels-to-be-fused for index-K, then 3 kernels for indexer, then 8 tiny kernels-to-be-fused for K and V. After fix: 1 fused Triton launch (contains previous 12 kernels for K, V and K-index), then 3 kernels for indexer. So it's fuse + reorder: compute the page/offset once, write K + V + index-K together, before the indexer runs. ## PR Checklist Please review the following before submitting your PR: - PR description clearly explains what and why. If using CodeRabbit's summary, please make sure it makes sense. - PR Follows [TRT-LLM CODING GUIDELINES](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/CODING_GUIDELINES.md) to the best of your knowledge. - Test cases are provided for new code paths (see [test instructions](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/tree/main/tests#1-how-does-the-ci-work)) - If PR introduces API changes, an appropriate PR label is added - either `api-compatible` or `api-breaking`. Documentation updated as needed - Update [tava architecture diagram](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/.github/tava_architecture_diagram.md) if there is a significant design change in PR. - The reviewers assigned automatically/manually are appropriate for the PR. - [x] Please check this after reviewing the above items as appropriate for this PR. ## GitHub Bot Help To see a list of available CI bot commands, please comment `/bot help`. ## Dev Engineer Review - Adds a Triton fused write for K, V, and optional index-K caches. - Updates metadata, model, and indexer paths to prevent duplicate writes. - Preserves legacy writes for unsupported inputs. - Main risks are cache layout, dtype conversion, device placement, marker reset, and fallback correctness. - Reported benchmarks show fewer launches and improved decode performance. ## QA Engineer Review - Modifies `test_msa_backend.py`. - Adds CPU input and slot-mapping cases that verify rejection without cache changes. - Existing coverage includes valid and invalid layouts, strides, dtypes, head sizes, empty writes, and optional index-K. - The test has a waiver entry, but no dedicated CI or manual-QA registration was found. - items.title: [None][feat] Attribute KV-cache hits to storage tiers in metrics (gpu/host/disk/remote)
items.body:
# [None][feat] Attribute KV-cache hits to storage tiers in metrics (gpu / host / disk / remote)


## Description

**Problem.** With host offloading (`host_cache_size`) a prefix-cache hit can be served from GPU
memory or copied back from host memory (or disk / an external store), but `kv_cache_hit_rate`,
`kv_cache_iter_reused_blocks_total` and `prompt_cached_tokens_total` report one aggregate.
`kv_cache_host_utilization` says how full the host pool is, not whether it served anything, and
`kv_cache_onboard_bytes_total` cannot be used to reconstruct hits because blocks also move on
resume after preemption and on prefetch. Operators cannot answer "is CPU offloading paying off",
and benchmark harnesses that price cached vs. uncached tokens get no tier information.

**Solution.** The KV cache manager attributes every reused block to the tier it was served from
at the moment the block is matched, before any onboard copy, and the split is exported end to end:

- Schema: `KvCacheStats::reusedBlocks{Gpu,Host,Disk,Remote}`,
  `KvCacheIterationStats::iterReusedBlocks{Gpu,Host,Disk,Remote}`, the same four fields on
  `executor::KvCacheStats` (JSON + binary serialization, nanobind), `KvCacheTier` enum shared
  with Python (`tensorrt_llm/metrics/enums.py::CACHE_TIER_LABELS`).
- `KVCacheManager` (C++): tier decided in `onboardAndAllocateBlocks` before `onboardBlock()`
  (`isPrimary()` on the matched block / partial-copy source; secondary is `host` for transfer mode
  DRAM and `disk` for GDS/POSIX). Connector-matched whole blocks move from missed to
  reused(`remote`) so aggregate hit rate and tier split agree. Per request the manager records
  ordered `(tier, tokens)` runs for the window that bounds the prepopulated length
  (`LlmRequest.reuse_tier_segments`).
- `KVCacheManagerV2`: per attention life cycle, reused blocks are split by `page.cache_level`; the
  request segments use the worst level among the life cycles that load a block, and `none` for
  blocks outside every sliding window (skipped by reuse, nothing loaded).
- Python: `LlmRequest.cached_tokens_by_tier` derives the request-level split from the segments
  and the latched `cached_tokens`, so the two request counters agree by construction. The split
  travels with the response (`LlmResult.cached_tokens_by_tier`) into
  `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens_details`, including through disaggregated serving
  (`ctx_usage` and the KV-transfer aux buffer).
- Prometheus (`MetricsCollector`):
  - `trtllm_kv_cache_reused_blocks_by_tier_total{cache_tier}` — sums to
    `trtllm_kv_cache_iter_reused_blocks_total`
  - `trtllm_prompt_cached_tokens_by_tier_total{cache_tier}` — sums to
    `trtllm_prompt_cached_tokens_total` for every request that carried an attribution
  - all `cache_tier` values pre-seeded to 0; no existing metric changes shape.
- Warmup: per-iteration KV deltas accumulated during warmup are drained after warmup, so the
  iteration counters start from the same point as the already-baselined cumulative counters.
- Docs: `docs/source/features/kvcache.md`, "Cache Hit Metrics by Storage Tier" (semantics,
  invariants, warmup, disagg, per-manager tier meaning).

Behavior changes to note: (1) with a KV cache connector, whole connector-filled blocks now count
as reuse (`remote`) instead of misses, so `kv_cache_hit_rate` reflects avoided recomputation;
(2) `kv_cache_iter_*` counters no longer include warmup dummy requests.

## Test Coverage

- `tests/unittest/metrics/test_collector.py::TestCacheTierMetrics` — pre-seeding, request split
  sums to aggregate, no guessing without attribution, `none` tier, V1 window and V2 lifecycle
  block aggregation.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/executor/test_kv_cache_tier_split.py` — segment-to-dict split, prefix
  trimming, sum invariant.
- `tests/unittest/kv_cache_manager_v2_tests/test_kv_cache_tier_attribution.py` — V2 gpu / host /
  none attribution against the runtime manager (host hits cross-checked with onboard traffic).
- `cpp/tests/unit_tests/batch_manager/kvCacheManagerTest.cpp` —
  `KVCacheManagerReuseTierAttributionGpuTest`, `KVCacheManagerReuseTierAttributionHostTest`.
- End-to-end (manual, script in the PR discussion): trtllm-serve with a 4096-token GPU pool and a
  host cache, prompt A -> fillers -> prompt A again shows `cache_tier="host"` hits for both
  managers and matching `cached_tokens_details` in the response usage.

## PR Checklist
- [x] PR description clearly explains what and why.
- [x] Follows TRT-LLM CODING GUIDELINES.
- [x] Test cases provided for new code paths.
- [x] Documentation updated.

items.title: [None][perf] Equal-cost context chunking for the KV cache V2 scheduler
items.body:
@coderabbitai summary

## Description

**Problem.** On hybrid-attention models (a few full-attention layers + many linear-attention layers, e.g. Kimi-K3 with 24 MLA + 69 KDA layers), a context iteration costs roughly `c0 + c1·N + c2·Σ(N_i·KV_i)`: the linear/MoE work scales with the scheduled token count `N`, while the full-attention layers additionally scale with each chunk's KV history depth. Under attention-DP the token budget (`max_num_tokens`) gives every rank the same `N` per iteration, but a rank holding a deep-KV request runs a far more expensive iteration, and lockstep collectives make all other ranks wait for it. On an AgentX agentic trace-replay benchmark (Kimi-K3 NVFP4, DEP16 ctx-only disagg, concurrency 128, heavy-tailed prompt distribution: p50 75k / p99 596k / max 970k tokens), a fitted per-iteration cost model shows **~45% of DP GPU time going to this straggler wait** (measured per-rank iteration time `T(N=8192, kv) = 1465 ms + 8.62 µs·kv`, i.e. a full-budget chunk at kv=996k runs 3.9× longer than at kv=130k).

**Solution: equal-cost context chunking (opt-in, default off).** The V2 scheduler's `BudgetTracker` gains an optional *cost* budget alongside the token budget. A context chunk of `n` tokens starting at KV position `kv_start` is charged `(kv_cost_offset + kv_start)·n`, and chunks are capped so the per-iteration total fits `B = (kv_cost_offset + kv_depth_threshold)·max_num_tokens`:

- `kv_cost_offset = c1/c2` converts the KV-independent per-token work into kv-token equivalents (fitted 140k for K3; a structural FLOPs estimate gives 136k).
- Requests shallower than `kv_depth_threshold` keep full-size chunks — the token cap binds first — so only the deep tail shrinks (e.g. kv=500k → 2560-token chunks).
- `B` is a constant shared by all DP ranks, so per-rank *predicted* iteration times equalize with **zero cross-rank coordination** — the same contract as `max_num_tokens` today, just denominated in predicted time instead of tokens.
- Leftover cost budget backfills subsequent (cheaper) requests via the existing SKIP semantics; a head-of-line floor of one chunk unit prevents starvation of very deep requests.
- Enabled via `TLLM_V2_CTX_COST_KV_OFFSET` / `TLLM_V2_CTX_COST_KV_DEPTH_THRESHOLD` (both required). Unset → the code path is inert and scheduling is bit-exact with today. TODO noted in-code: promote to a scheduler config field and calibrate `kv_cost_offset` online from measured iteration times.

**A/B results** (Kimi-K3 NVFP4, 8×GB300, ctx-only disagg DEP16, AgentX traces, concurrency 128, 1800 s measurement, `kv_cost_offset=140000 kv_depth_threshold=64000`; control = identical build with the env vars unset):

| metric | control | treatment | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| effective prefill throughput | 324,986 tok/s | 385,395 tok/s | **+18.6%** |
| request throughput | 2.57 req/s | 3.20 req/s | **+24.5%** |
| TTFT p50 / p90 | 39.5 s / 189.6 s | 24.5 s / 125.6 s | **−38% / −34%** |
| TTFT p99 | 532.9 s | 827.0 s | +55% (see below) |
| per-rank iter-time p90/p50 spread | 1.67 | 1.15 | equalization |
| prompt cache hit (sanity) | 94.26% | 94.59% | unchanged |

Measured chunk sizes match the formula to within one alignment unit across the whole KV range (kv 100–200k → 5888 vs theory 5762; 400–500k → 2816 vs 2832; 800–900k → 1728 vs 1688). The known trade-off: the deepest ~1% requests no longer monopolize a full token budget every iteration, so *their own* TTFT grows — in exchange, in the control the p99 tail was innocent requests queued behind a monster that monopolized one rank for 117 consecutive iterations (852 s); in the treatment that monopoly pattern disappears entirely. Mitigations for the deep requests themselves (per-request cost-share floor, context-parallel prefill) are follow-up work.

## Calibration

`examples/scheduler_cost_calibration/fit_context_cost.py` derives both knobs from the per-rank iteration log of an ordinary token-budget run (`TLLM_PROFILE_LOG_RANKS=all`, ~30 min): `kv_cost_offset` via monopoly-span Theil–Sen (robust to eviction-stall outliers, with a piecewise-linearity diagnostic — measured per-band slopes agree within ±4% from kv 8k to 954k), `kv_depth_threshold` as a percentile of the token-weighted KV-depth distribution. It also reports the measured lockstep waste and the predicted gain, so users can tell whether the feature is worth enabling before touching anything. Two independent DEP16 runs reproduce each other's fit within the stated uncertainty (kv_cost_offset 114k vs 140k, kv_depth_threshold 60k vs 64k)

items.title: [#18156][fix] Carry lora_id and share the cache_salt derivation in the KV-aware router
items.body:
## Description

Fixes #18156.

The KV-cache-aware router scores workers by recomputing a request's block hashes and matching them against the hashes workers publish in KV cache events. `KvCacheAwareServerState.matched_tokens` walks a request's block-hash list and breaks on the first miss, so any first-block mismatch makes `match_count` 0 for the whole request: cache-aware routing silently degrades to load balancing, with no error and no log line.

Two request dimensions never survived that recomputation.

**`lora_id` was dropped entirely.** `hash_v1_block_key` already accepts `lora_task_id` and the worker supplies it from `ReuseScope.lora_id` (`_event_manager._hash_block_key`), but nothing under `tensorrt_llm/serve/` ever passed it: `grep -i lora tensorrt_llm/serve/router_utils.py tensorrt_llm/serve/router.py` had zero hits. So every LoRA request scored zero matches, and because all adapters hashed identically, the router's own prefix accounting collided adapters with one another. This change adds `_get_request_lora_id` next to the existing `_get_request_cache_salt_id` and threads the adapter id through `block_key_hasher`, `v2_sha256_block_hasher`, `_compute_block_hashes`, the `_tokenize_and_compute_block_hashes*` helpers and `ReuseScope`. The native `BlockKeyHasher` fast path takes no lora id, so it is skipped when one is set, exactly as it already is for a salt.

**The salt id was derived twice.** The router used blake3 (`kv_cache_hash.get_cache_salt_id`) while the V2 engine used sha256 (`KVCacheManagerV2._derive_reuse_salt`), so a salted request could not match a V2 worker either. This keeps the engine's derivation and makes it the single source of truth both sides import; the engine's published ids are unchanged, so nothing a running worker has already emitted moves. The V1 C++ `BlockKeyHasher` mixes `std::hash<std::string>(cacheSalt)` directly, which is implementation-defined and not reproducible in Python; that limitation is now documented on the shared helper rather than left implicit.

It also removes the duplicate `get_cache_salt_id` in `tensorrt_llm/inputs/utils.py`. It had no engine caller, and `test_cache_salt_id_derivation_matches_worker_path` pinned the router against *it* — so the parity test passed while the two live derivations disagreed. The test now pins against `KVCacheManagerV2._derive_reuse_salt`.

Scope note: this is one concern (the router's reuse-namespace keying) in one component; the engine-side keying was already correct and is untouched apart from delegating its derivation.

## Test Coverage

`tests/unittest/disaggregated/test_router.py`:

- `test_router_block_hashes_round_trip_worker_event_hashes` — new, parametrized over {no salt, salt} x {no lora, lora} for all three hash algorithms. The worker side runs the real published-hash path (`KVCacheEventManager._v1_hash_from_radix_block`) over a radix chain seeded with the worker's `ReuseScope`, and asserts the router computes the same hashes. This fails on `main` for every arm except the unsalted/unadapted one.
- `test_cache_salt_id_derivation_matches_worker_path` — re-pinned to the engine's derivation, plus the `None` case.
- `test_get_request_lora_id_extraction` — new, covers the object and dict request shapes and the absent case.

The reproducer from #18156 runs on CPU with no bindings and no GPU, and reproduces the before/after directly. On `main`, a LoRA request gives worker `1405807694910447675` vs router `924206229973855` and 0/8 block overlap; with this change both sides produce `1405807694910447675`. For a salted request the v2 root key was `ceb640ee7c220334` on the worker vs `982186b7060809a3` on the router; both are now `ceb640ee7c220334`.

Run on an RTX A6000 against the `tensorrt_llm==1.3.0rc24` wheel (the newest published wheel; the repo's `conftest.py` needs `tensorrt_llm.executor.ray`, which postdates it, so the file was run with `--noconftest` -- every fixture it uses is defined in the test file):

```
new tests, unpatched library:   6 failed, 85 deselected
new tests, patched library:     6 passed, 85 deselected
full router suite, patched:    91 passed
full router suite, pristine:    6 failed, 85 passed
```

So the new tests fail on `main` for every arm except the unsalted/unadapted one, pass with the change, and the 85 pre-existing tests are unaffected.

`pre-commit run --files <changed files>` passes.

items.title: [TRTLLM-12891][feat] Support v2_kvcm-exclusive budgeting capabilty for the KV cache connector
items.body:
Depending upon #18762. Landing it first as the non-API breaking implementation to allow users to leverage KV connector+v2_kvcm with backward-compatibility of existing usages.

## Description

Real allocation was done by the v2_kvcm during scheduling and the scheduled request can possibly be refuted during proceeding checks until the final batch for the iteration is finalized. The v2_kvcm allows a request to be `SUSPENDED` which made this possible. This capability is not available for the v1_kvcm. Such scheduling behavior is the `MAX_UTILIZATION` scheduling policy that leads to better budgeting and leads to better utilization rate of the GPU (implying better throughput).

This MR allows the KV connector to contribute along with the local radix tree during scheduling, which allows saving by the connector be accounted during budgeting and improve utilization.

For user to leverage this, there will be two main actions for the user:
- The connector setup needs to be toggled "aggressive".
- The cancalation callback action of the KV connector needs to be implemented

**(Backward compatibility)** Without turning the knob to aggressize, the connector will not provide its prefix contribution to scheduler's budgeting. This preserves the original users' connector code to still work as-is.

```
Connector's actions and where it is called according to conservative/aggressive:  

  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┐
  │                               Phase                                │ Conservative (18762, default) │     Aggressive (new, opt-in)      │
  ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 1 — ask (query_num_new_matched_tokens)                             │ prepare_resources             │ prepare_context (scheduling pass) │
  ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 2 — reserve pages, advance context_current_position                │ prepare_resources             │ prepare_context                   │
  ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 3 — deliver (commit_new_matched_tokens) + update_state_after_alloc │ prepare_resources             │ prepare_resources                 │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────────┘
```

**[JIRA ticket/NVBugs ID/GitHub issue/None][type] Summary**

Valid ticket formats:

Valid types (lowercase): [fix], [feat], [doc], [infra], [chore], etc.

Examples:
  - [TRTLLM-1234][feat] Add new feature
  - [https://nvbugs/1234567][fix] Fix some bugs
  - [#1234][doc] Update documentation
  - [None][chore] Minor clean-up

Alternative (faster) way using CodeRabbit AI:

**[JIRA ticket/NVBugs ID/GitHub issue/None] @coderabbitai title**

NOTE: "@coderabbitai title" will be replaced by the title generated by CodeRabbit AI, that includes the "[type]" and title.
For more info, see /.coderabbit.yaml.

-->

## Description

<!--
Please explain the issue and the solution in short.
-->

This pull request introduces support for pipelined KV cache transfer, allowing each prefill chunk to be transferred as soon as it is computed, rather than waiting for the entire prompt to finish. The changes add chunk-aware block projection utilities, update session and metadata handling for chunked transfers, and include compatibility checks to ensure pipelined transfer is only enabled in supported configurations. Several internal APIs and behaviors are updated to support chunked transfer, error propagation, and session management.

**Pipelined KV Cache Transfer Support:**

* Added the `project_blocks_to_chunk` function to efficiently project block IDs to the current chunk, enabling chunked transfer of KV cache blocks. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-337dabe32d190384907e8c1330d67ed73ff63f41fbf0c1a347ff9f2ad18d4590R151-R171) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3cab8f284e64d42a9c7004535a761cabcdc7323d787ddbecdbd467b7e4f935b9R698-R770)
* Introduced the `pipeline_transfer_enabled` property and `has_inflight_transfer` method to indicate and manage pipelined transfer state. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3cab8f284e64d42a9c7004535a761cabcdc7323d787ddbecdbd467b7e4f935b9R698-R770) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d9a5e6c78d3e0e8e3d04ed0a22f880c00dd171b1535ba542835b5c5e473817a4R239-R250)
* Implemented the `_build_prefill_chunk` method to construct KV slices for each prefill chunk and updated `respond_and_send_async` to use chunked slices when pipelined transfer is enabled.

**Session and Metadata Handling:**

* Updated the `WriteMeta` dataclass and related logic to track both sender and receiver slice IDs, ensuring correct addressing for chunked transfers. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-337dabe32d190384907e8c1330d67ed73ff63f41fbf0c1a347ff9f2ad18d4590R185-R188) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-337dabe32d190384907e8c1330d67ed73ff63f41fbf0c1a347ff9f2ad18d4590L580-R605) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-337dabe32d190384907e8c1330d67ed73ff63f41fbf0c1a347ff9f2ad18d4590L610-R635) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-337dabe32d190384907e8c1330d67ed73ff63f41fbf0c1a347ff9f2ad18d4590L654-R679) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-337dabe32d190384907e8c1330d67ed73ff63f41fbf0c1a347ff9f2ad18d4590R1000)
* Improved session status handling to immediately mark sessions as failed if any chunk encounters an error, preventing sessions from being stuck in an incomplete state.

**Compatibility and Error Handling:**

* Added strict compatibility checks to ensure pipelined transfer is only enabled when pipeline parallelism is 1, bounce buffer is disabled, and non-Mamba cache managers are used.
* Enhanced cancellation and session cleanup logic to avoid premature deletion of requests and to handle pipelined session lifetimes correctly. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3cab8f284e64d42a9c7004535a761cabcdc7323d787ddbecdbd467b7e4f935b9R624-R628) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3cab8f284e64d42a9c7004535a761cabcdc7323d787ddbecdbd467b7e4f935b9L977-R1070) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-f0b4c3c02708916fd189f863c48b982a55f34ae94996089b23aa0a6f0571fe19R7476-R7478)

**Block and Slice Management:**

* Updated `_create_kv_slice` to support resident block bounds and ensure only computed blocks are included in chunked transfers, with correct handling of scratch, stale, and reused blocks. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3cab8f284e64d42a9c7004535a761cabcdc7323d787ddbecdbd467b7e4f935b9L262-R284) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3cab8f284e64d42a9c7004535a761cabcdc7323d787ddbecdbd467b7e4f935b9L295) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-3cab8f284e64d42a9c7004535a761cabcdc7323d787ddbecdbd467b7e4f935b9L320-R337) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-3cab8f284e64d42a9c7004535a761cabcdc7323d787ddbecdbd467b7e4f935b9R346-R368)
* Modified block trimming and projection logic to work with chunked and partial slices, ensuring correctness for both full and partial prompt transfers.

**API and Import Updates:**

* Exported `project_blocks_to_chunk` for use in transceiver logic and updated imports accordingly.

These changes collectively enable and robustly support pipelined KV cache transfer, improving efficiency for large prompt handling while maintaining correctness and error resilience.

items.body:
## Summary
- **Root cause**: One-engine MTP built a second `DeepseekV4CacheManager` as draft manager, but `_num_tables` is assigned only by `compute_sliding_block_tables()`, which the DSv4 metadata calls on the target manager alone — leaving the draft instance uninitialized.
- **Fix**: Suppress the separate draft KV cache manager for the `deepseek_v4` algorithm via an algorithm-keyed predicate in `config_utils.py` (kept out of `llm_args.py`, which is confscan rc=1 at pristine main), with `sparse_attention_config` made a required parameter so all three call sites thread it.
- **Original test**: `pytest tests/integration/defs/perf/test_perf.py --perf --test-list=.repair-bot/perf_test_list.txt --output-dir=build/perf_output -v`
- Automated fix generated by repair-bot

## Test plan
- [x] Verify fix on the same GPU type as the original failure
- [x] Check for regressions in related tests

## Links
- Bug: https://nvbugs/6627033


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Dev Engineer Review

- The fix disables the separate draft KV-cache manager for `deepseek_v4`.
- The new `is_deepseek_v4_sparse` helper uses the configured algorithm key.
- `sparse_attention_config` now propagates through all call sites.
- DSA keeps its separate manager because it overrides `copy_batch_block_offsets`.
- The API changes are consistent across declarations and callers.
- No configuration files or test-list files changed.
- No unintended performance or scope changes were identified.

## QA Engineer Review
